extracted_claims.text: Article 43 of the EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689) sets out the conformity assessment procedures that providers of high-risk AI systems must follow before placing a system on the market.

For high-risk AI systems listed in Annex III, Article 43 provides two possible routes: internal control conformity assessment under Annex VI, or assessment of the quality management system and technical documentation by a notified body under Annex VII.

Annex VII (notified body) assessment is mandatory for high-risk biometric identification systems (point 1 of Annex III) and is generally required for certain critical infrastructure AI systems, whereas most other high-risk AI systems under Annex III can use the Annex VI self-assessment route.

For high-risk AI systems that are safety components of products covered by sectoral Union harmonisation legislation listed in Section A of Annex I (e.g. medical devices, machinery), the provider must follow the conformity assessment procedure of that sectoral legislation, with notified bodies additionally verifying compliance with the AI-specific requirements.

A new conformity assessment is required if a high-risk AI system is substantially modified, except for changes that were predetermined by the provider at the time of the initial conformity assessment (relevant to systems that continue to learn after deployment).

For the purposes of the conformity assessment procedure under Annex VII, the provider may generally choose any notified body; however, where a high-risk AI system is intended to be put into service by law enforcement, immigration or asylum authorities, or by EU institutions, bodies, offices or agencies, the relevant market surveillance authority acts as the notified body instead.

Article 46 allows a market surveillance authority, by way of derogation from Article 43 and upon a duly justified request, to authorise the placing on the market or putting into service of specific high-risk AI systems without the standard conformity assessment, for a limited period, for exceptional reasons of public security, protection of life and health, environmental protection, or protection of key industrial/infrastructural assets.

Article 44 governs certificates issued following conformity assessment, Article 45 sets information obligations for notified bodies, Article 47 requires an EU declaration of conformity, Article 48 requires CE marking, and Article 35 governs identification numbers and lists of notified bodies.

The Commission may adopt delegated acts under Article 43(5), per Article 97, to update Annex VI and Annex VII conformity assessment procedures in light of technical progress, without needing to revise the AI Act itself.
Notified bodies for the AI Act are to be listed in the Commission's NANDO (New Approach Notified and Designated Organisations) database, similar to the system used for medical devices under MDR/IVDR.

As of October 2025, NANDO listed 51 MDR-designated notified bodies and 19 IVDR-designated notified bodies, but these are designations under the Medical Devices Regulation/In Vitro Diagnostic Regulation, not the AI Act.

As of March 2026, no notified bodies had yet been designated specifically for AI Act conformity assessments; designation processes were described as still ongoing across Member States with limited capacity.
As of April 2026, no notified bodies had been formally designated under the AI Act in the context of medical device AI (MDR/IVDR interplay).

High-risk AI obligations under the AI Act are stated to fully apply from August 2026 (with one source citing August 2, 2026 as the deadline for SaaS providers to issue declarations of conformity), and notified bodies designated under the AI Act are expected to begin conducting AI Act-specific conformity assessments only after 2026.

A Commission proposal (COM(2025) 836) and an associated Council document (ST-7322-2026-INIT) propose a new Annex XIV listing codes and categories of AI systems for notified body designation scope under NANDO, and propose amendments to Regulation (EU) 2018/1139 to integrate AI Act high-risk requirements, but this measure is presented as a legislative proposal rather than adopted law.

Separately, under the Cyber Resilience Act (a different EU regulation, not the AI Act), zero notified bodies had been designated in NANDO as of late June 2026, with a target of sufficient notified body capacity by 11 December 2026 and full application from 11 December 2027.

open_issues: No source confirms that any notified bodies have been formally designated specifically for AI Act conformity assessments as of the research date (October 2026); available sources only report the absence of designations as of March/April 2026.

It is unclear whether the Commission proposal in COM(2025) 836 / ST-7322-2026-INIT (new Annex XIV, NANDO codes, amendments to Regulation 2018/1139) has been formally adopted or remains in the legislative pipeline as of October 2026.
The sources do not specify a current, dated list of which notified bodies (if any) have since been designated under the AI Act between April 2026 and October 2026.

It is unclear how the Annex VI/Annex VII self-assessment vs. notified-body split interacts in practice with the sectoral conformity assessment route under Annex I Section A products, e.g., whether both a sectoral notified body and an AI Act-specific notified body role are needed.

The precise boundary between which Annex III categories require mandatory notified body (Annex VII) assessment versus optional Annex VI self-assessment is only partially detailed in the sources (clearly biometric identification is called out, but full categorization across all Annex III points is not fully confirmed by official sources in this set).

It is unclear what happens in practice for providers facing the August 2026 compliance deadline given the reported lack of designated notified bodies, i.e., how conformity assessment obligations are being enforced given capacity shortfalls.
report:
# Conformity Assessment Procedures for High-Risk AI Systems Under the EU AI Act

## Executive Summary
Article 43 of the EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689) establishes two main conformity assessment routes for high-risk AI systems—internal control (Annex VI) and third-party notified body assessment (Annex VII)—with the applicable route depending on the system's classification and sector ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43)). According to low-confidence, non-authoritative blog sources, no notified bodies had been formally designated for AI Act-specific assessments as of early-to-mid 2026, raising open questions about enforcement capacity as the August 2026 deadline approaches ([eyreACT](https://eyreact.com/notified-bodies-ai-act); [AIAct Navigator](https://aiact-navigator.com/blog/eu-ai-act-medical-devices-mdr-ivdr-interplay-guide)).

## Key Findings

### Legal Framework for Conformity Assessment
Article 43 of the AI Act sets out the conformity assessment procedures providers of high-risk AI systems must complete before market placement (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43)). For Annex III high-risk systems, providers may generally choose between internal control assessment under Annex VI or notified-body assessment of the quality management system and technical documentation under Annex VII (low confidence) ([DPO Consulting](https://www.dpo-consulting.com/blog/ai-conformity-assessment); [FPF](https://fpf.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/OT-comformity-assessment-under-the-eu-ai-act-WP-1.pdf)). Reporting suggests Annex VII notified-body assessment is mandatory for biometric identification systems (Annex III, point 1) and generally required for certain critical infrastructure systems, while most other Annex III categories may use Annex VI self-assessment, though this categorization is only partially confirmed by official sources (low confidence) ([Quantamix Solutions](https://quantamixsolutions.com/insights/eu-ai-act-conformity-assessment); [Openlayer](https://www.openlayer.com/blog/eu-ai-act-compliance-checklist-high-risk-systems)).

For high-risk AI systems that are safety components of products under sectoral EU harmonisation legislation (e.g., medical devices, machinery) listed in Annex I Section A, providers must follow that sector's conformity assessment procedure, with notified bodies additionally verifying AI-specific requirements (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43); [VDE](https://www.vde.com/topics-en/artificial-intelligence/blog/conformity-assessment-high-risk-ai)).

A new conformity assessment is required after substantial modification of a high-risk system, except for changes predetermined by the provider at initial assessment—relevant to continuously-learning systems (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43)). Providers may generally select any notified body for Annex VII assessments, except where systems are intended for use by law enforcement, immigration, asylum authorities, or EU institutions, in which case the relevant market surveillance authority performs this role instead (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/ga/ai-act/article-43)). Article 46 permits market surveillance authorities to derogate from standard assessment requirements for limited periods under exceptional public security, health, environmental, or infrastructural circumstances (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-46)).

Related provisions include Article 44 (certificates), Article 45 (notified body information obligations), Article 47 (EU declaration of conformity), Article 48 (CE marking), and Article 35 (identification numbers and notified body lists), with Article 16 setting related obligations on providers of high-risk systems (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk - Article 60](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-60); [AI Act Service Desk - Article 16](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-16); [regulation-ai.eu](https://www.regulation-ai.eu/en/articles/article-35)).

### Notified Body Designation Status
Notified bodies for the AI Act are to be listed in the Commission's NANDO database, mirroring the system used under the Medical Devices Regulation/IVDR (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02017R0745-20260101); [regulation-ai.eu](https://www.regulation-ai.eu/en/articles/article-35)). As of October 2025, NANDO listed 51 MDR-designated and 19 IVDR-designated notified bodies—but these designations are under MDR/IVDR, not the AI Act itself (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A52025SC1051)). Industry sources report that, as of March and April 2026 respectively, no notified bodies had yet been formally designated specifically for AI Act assessments, with designation processes described as ongoing and capacity-constrained across Member States (low confidence) ([eyreACT](https://eyreact.com/notified-bodies-ai-act); [AIAct Navigator](https://aiact-navigator.com/blog/eu-ai-act-medical-devices-mdr-ivdr-interplay-guide)).

### Timeline and Pending Legislative Developments
High-risk AI obligations are stated to fully apply from August 2026, with one source citing August 2, 2026 as the deadline for SaaS providers to issue declarations of conformity (low confidence) ([sota.io](https://sota.io/blog/eu-ai-act-eu-declaration-conformity-ce-marking-registration-saas-providers-2026)). A Commission proposal (COM(2025) 836) and Council document (ST-7322-2026-INIT) propose a new Annex XIV listing NANDO designation codes and amendments integrating AI Act requirements into aviation regulation (2018/1139), but this remains a legislative proposal, not adopted law (medium confidence) ([Council of the EU](https://data.consilium.europa.eu/doc/document/ST-7322-2026-INIT/en/pdf)).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
No direct contradictions were identified among sources. However, several low-confidence claims warrant caution: the specific March/April 2026 statements that no notified bodies had been designated ([eyreACT](https://eyreact.com/notified-bodies-ai-act); [AIAct Navigator](https://aiact-navigator.com/blog/eu-ai-act-medical-devices-mdr-ivdr-interplay-guide)) rely solely on non-authoritative blog sources rather than official EU confirmation. The claimed delegated-act power under Article 43(5)/97 is scored very low confidence (0.03) and lacks corroboration.

## Knowledge Gaps
It remains unclear whether any notified bodies have been designated under the AI Act since April 2026, and whether the COM(2025) 836 proposal (new Annex XIV) has been adopted. The precise Annex III categorization determining mandatory notified-body versus self-assessment routes is incompletely documented. How conformity assessment obligations will be enforced given the apparent lack of designated bodies ahead of the August 2026 deadline is unresolved, as is the interplay between sectoral and AI Act-specific notified body roles for Annex I Section A products.

# Conformity Assessment Procedures for High-Risk AI Systems Under the EU AI Act

## Executive Summary
Article 43 of the EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689) establishes two main conformity assessment routes for high-risk AI systems—internal control (Annex VI) and third-party notified body assessment (Annex VII)—with the applicable route depending on the system's classification and sector ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43)). Despite high-risk obligations being set to fully apply from August 2026, no notified bodies had been formally designated for AI Act-specific assessments as of early-to-mid 2026, raising open questions about enforcement capacity as the deadline approaches ([eyreACT](https://eyreact.com/notified-bodies-ai-act); [AIAct Navigator](https://aiact-navigator.com/blog/eu-ai-act-medical-devices-mdr-ivdr-interplay-guide)).

## Key Findings

### Legal Framework for Conformity Assessment
Article 43 of the AI Act sets out the conformity assessment procedures providers of high-risk AI systems must complete before market placement (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43)). For Annex III high-risk systems, providers may generally choose between internal control assessment under Annex VI or notified-body assessment of the quality management system and technical documentation under Annex VII (low confidence) ([DPO Consulting](https://www.dpo-consulting.com/blog/ai-conformity-assessment); [FPF](https://fpf.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/OT-comformity-assessment-under-the-eu-ai-act-WP-1.pdf)). Reporting suggests Annex VII notified-body assessment is mandatory for biometric identification systems (Annex III, point 1) and generally required for certain critical infrastructure systems, while most other Annex III categories may use Annex VI self-assessment, though this categorization is only partially confirmed by official sources (low confidence) ([Quantamix Solutions](https://quantamixsolutions.com/insights/eu-ai-act-conformity-assessment)).

For high-risk AI systems that are safety components of products under sectoral EU harmonisation legislation (e.g., medical devices, machinery) listed in Annex I Section A, providers must follow that sector's conformity assessment procedure, with notified bodies additionally verifying AI-specific requirements (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43); [VDE](https://www.vde.com/topics-en/artificial-intelligence/blog/conformity-assessment-high-risk-ai)).

A new conformity assessment is required after substantial modification of a high-risk system, except for changes predetermined by the provider at initial assessment—relevant to continuously-learning systems (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43)). Providers may generally select any notified body for Annex VII assessments, except where systems are intended for use by law enforcement, immigration, asylum authorities, or EU institutions, in which case the relevant market surveillance authority performs this role instead (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/ga/ai-act/article-43)). Article 46 permits market surveillance authorities to derogate from standard assessment requirements for limited periods under exceptional public security, health, environmental, or infrastructural circumstances (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-46)).

Related provisions include Article 44 (certificates), Article 45 (notified body information obligations), Article 47 (EU declaration of conformity), Article 48 (CE marking), and Article 35 (identification numbers and notified body lists) (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-60); [regulation-ai.eu](https://www.regulation-ai.eu/en/articles/article-35)).

### Notified Body Designation Status
Notified bodies for the AI Act are to be listed in the Commission's NANDO database, mirroring the system used under the Medical Devices Regulation/IVDR (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02017R0745-20260101); [regulation-ai.eu](https://www.regulation-ai.eu/en/articles/article-35)). As of October 2025, NANDO listed 51 MDR-designated and 19 IVDR-designated notified bodies—but these designations are under MDR/IVDR, not the AI Act itself (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A52025SC1051)). Industry sources report that, as of March and April 2026 respectively, no notified bodies had yet been formally designated specifically for AI Act assessments, with designation processes described as ongoing and capacity-constrained across Member States (low confidence) ([eyreACT](https://eyreact.com/notified-bodies-ai-act); [AIAct Navigator](https://aiact-navigator.com/blog/eu-ai-act-medical-devices-mdr-ivdr-interplay-guide)).

### Timeline and Pending Legislative Developments
High-risk AI obligations are stated to fully apply from August 2026, with one source citing August 2, 2026 as the deadline for SaaS providers to issue declarations of conformity (low confidence) ([sota.io](https://sota.io/blog/eu-ai-act-eu-declaration-conformity-ce-marking-registration-saas-providers-2026)). A Commission proposal (COM(2025) 836) and Council document (ST-7322-2026-INIT) propose a new Annex XIV listing NANDO designation codes and amendments integrating AI Act requirements into aviation regulation (2018/1139), but this remains a legislative proposal, not adopted law (medium confidence) ([Council of the EU](https://data.consilium.europa.eu/doc/document/ST-7322-2026-INIT/en/pdf)).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
No direct contradictions were identified among sources. However, several low-confidence claims warrant caution: the specific March/April 2026 statements that no notified bodies had been designated ([eyreACT](https://eyreact.com/notified-bodies-ai-act); [AIAct Navigator](https://aiact-navigator.com/blog/eu-ai-act-medical-devices-mdr-ivdr-interplay-guide)) rely solely on non-authoritative blog sources rather than official EU confirmation. The claimed delegated-act power under Article 43(5)/97 is scored very low confidence (0.03) and lacks corroboration.

## Knowledge Gaps
It remains unclear whether any notified bodies have been designated under the AI Act since April 2026, and whether the COM(2025) 836 proposal (new Annex XIV) has been adopted. The precise Annex III categorization determining mandatory notified-body versus self-assessment routes is incompletely documented. How conformity assessment obligations will be enforced given the apparent lack of designated bodies ahead of the August 2026 deadline is unresolved, as is the interplay between sectoral and AI Act-specific notified body roles for Annex I Section A products.
